tasks.task: Write a one-page spec for an AI feature

items.when: Before any code or prompt, to agree what the feature does, how good it must be and how it fails
When the client wants goals, non-goals, success measures and acceptance checks in their usual format
When you want a second plan from data check to launch, with monitoring, to compare
When the request is vague and needs turning into clear steps and a fair test

tasks.task: Check whether the task needs AI at all

items.when: Before building, to see if a plain rule, lookup or form would do the job cheaper and safer
When you have ten or twenty real cases and want to see if one simple rule covers them
When the choice is between a model API, a tuned model or a bought tool, with the break-even

tasks.task: Build one AI feature into an app

items.when: When a client names one job for a model, or a feature needs rebuilding after complaints
When you write the feature: prompt in its own file, checked output, safe failure and limits
When the feature calls Claude and you need the API used the right way
When the feature calls OpenAI and you need current answers and the right model for the job
When calls can be rate limited and need safe waiting, retrying and backing off
When the code is written, to catch repeated logic and common AI coding mistakes
When you work inside the client's project and need changes made and tests run

tasks.task: Write a script that pulls structured data out of text

items.when: When fields must come out of emails, notes or forms as checked rows, with unsure ones flagged
When you need code that returns checked fields and retries when the reply does not fit
When you want a second way to get typed results, to compare on the same samples
When the source is scans or office files and the text must be read out first
Before it runs on real data, to score it on 15 to 30 real cases with known answers

tasks.task: Build an assistant that answers from the client's documents

items.when: When answers must come only from the client's documents, cite the section and admit gaps
Before building, to choose how to split, embed and store the documents and how to test results
When you want working code that answers from the files and shows which pages it used
When the documents need a store that finds passages by meaning
When answers are wrong and you must tell a retrieval fault from an answer fault

tasks.task: Design a prompt with a test set

items.when: When a prompt needs 15 to 30 realistic cases with pass rules before any wording is changed
When you want a second prompt draft and test cases from the task and answer format
When there are several versions and each needs a score on the same cases
When the tuned prompt must ship with saved versions and a way back
When scores are argued over and nobody has read the actual failing examples one by one

tasks.task: Fix a prompt that misbehaves and report what changed

items.when: When complaints are in and you must turn them into test cases before touching the prompt
When you have bad chats and approved help text and need wrong answers listed with retests
When a prompt gives weak or uneven answers and needs a tighter version
When hand tuning has stalled and a program that tunes its own prompts is worth a try
When you want test, fix and re-test run for you until the checks pass
When a change is proposed, to show what got better and what got worse on fixed cases

tasks.task: Write an evaluation script and a model grader

items.when: When some cases need judgement, such as tone or faithfulness, and a model must grade them the same way each time
Before the script, to plan scores, human review and side-by-side checks
When the grader needs a scoring guide with checks for its own bias
When the app needs test cases wired in so each change is compared on real results
When someone claims a change made the feature better and it must be proven

tasks.task: Review an AI feature or agent before launch

items.when: Before launch, to review the feature against the known risks for AI apps and tool servers
When the thing being launched is an agent that can take actions
When you need injection, jailbreak and tool abuse risks found and ranked
When the review finds gaps and rules must be added for refusals, made-up facts and leaked details
When some actions should wait for a person and you need clear rules for which ones
When the review covers normal use only and nobody has asked what happens when a step fails

tasks.task: Write and run prompt injection tests on your own feature

items.when: Before launching a chatbot, document assistant or agent you own, to write safe test inputs
When you need a map of where outside text reaches the model and what it could do
When tests fail and layered defences must be added in the code
When inputs need a small filter that flags hidden instructions before they land
When fixes are in and you need retest records and a list of control gaps
When you want injection and spending risks handled in one run, to compare with your plan

tasks.task: Estimate cost and set spending limits

items.when: Before launch or a model change, to estimate cost per call and per month, low and high
When the estimate is too high and you need where the tokens go and what to change
When code calls a paid model and needs caps and loop limits before a surprise bill
When every model call should check the budget first and record tokens and cost
When an agent needs budget reservations, hard stops and cost tracking in code

tasks.task: Add logging and monitoring to AI code

items.when: Before adding logs, to plan what to trace for steps, costs and errors without storing private data
When you want open tracing of every step with tests that score answers
When the team may prefer a hosted tracing tool with test sets and scores
When failures and cost spikes must raise an alert, not sit in a log

tasks.task: Run the AI feature health check after launch

items.when: Every two weeks for the first two months after launch, then monthly
When the test set must be rerun and new failures from real use added to it
When real cost per call should be set against the estimate
When the client must decide to widen, hold or stop and needs the evidence against the baseline

tasks.task: Review an AI feature after an incident

items.when: After a bad answer, a leak or a runaway bill, to find which control was missing
When you have the timeline and evidence and need a blameless report with owners
When the incident came from hidden instructions and the case must become a standing test

tasks.task: Build and check an MCP server

items.when: When an existing API should become a tool server others can install, start to finish
When you have an API spec and want the server written in Python or TypeScript
When there is no API spec and the tools must be described by hand, with tests
When a tool's description is vague and the model picks the wrong one or guesses inputs
When the server runs and you need to know if a model picks the right tool on real tasks
Before others install it, to trace risks through each tool handler
Before each release, to verify the package does what it says

tasks.task: Design an agent that uses tools safely

items.when: Before building, to settle the design and its trade-offs
When the job may need several agents, to see a design with handoffs and cost limits
When each tool needs a clear, safe definition the model can call without guessing
When the agent must remember things between steps or sessions
When some actions spend money or change records and need a person's yes
When the agent works and you need a safe test of where it can be tricked
Before the agent touches real accounts or data

tasks.task: Choose a model or plan a model change

items.when: When each candidate model needs its cost per call and per month side by side
When the same test set must be run on each model before any switch
When the new model needs prompt changes and you must see what got worse
When the client asks whether to tune a model of their own or stay on an API

tasks.task: Design a chatbot's conversation and fallbacks

items.when: When the bot needs flows with questions, error recovery and a graceful way out
When you want a working first version to try the flow on real questions
When the bot must answer only from approved text and say when it does not know
Before the bot faces the public, to test whether users can talk it out of its rules

tasks.task: Check privacy and AI rules for a feature

items.when: When the feature serves people in the EU and you need its risk tier and duties
When customer data goes to a model and you need the duties and the proof you lack
When you must show what data the feature sends, stores and logs

tasks.task: Build a batch job that runs a model over many records

items.when: When the job needs a prompt file, checked output and a safe way to skip bad records
When the job needs scheduling, checks and fixes for common faults around the model step
When thousands of calls will hit rate limits and must wait and retry safely
Before the first full run, to cap spend and stop a loop from running away

tasks.task: Review AI feature code and tests before merge

items.when: When an AI tool wrote much of the code and it needs a pass for common slips
When the change handles keys, user input or outside text and needs a bug and security review
When the review must also cover what the model can be made to do, not only the code

always.when: Before any code that calls a paid model runs unattended, to confirm caps and loop limits
Before any code is handed over, to catch common slips

helpers.when: When the feature needs new endpoints, queues or database changes around the model call
When the launch review finds risks that need a full security test of the app
When several prompts need designing and tuning at once across features
When the job is a customer-facing bot with handover to staff and a help centre behind it
When the documents or records need a proper pipeline before a model can use them
When the feature needs tests beyond the prompt, across the whole app

gaps: No library item estimates what an AI feature will cost per call and per month with a low and high case; only the kit prompt covers it
No library item decides between a plain rule and a model for a task; only the kit prompt covers it
No library item builds a test set from real logs with expected results and pass rules; only the kit skill covers it
No library item tests retrieval on its own: whether the right passage was found, and whether the assistant says it does not know
No library item plans a model change: rerun the test set on the new model, compare cost and quality, and roll back
No library item tunes prompt caching, batching or response time for a live feature
No library item removes personal details from text before it is sent to a model
No library item designs what happens when the model is down, slow or unsure, such as a queue for a person
No library item runs a regular health check on a live AI feature: sample logs, new failures and cost per call
No thinking lens in the library looks at a system the way an attacker would
